text:
A: Alright, mate! Can you hear me?
B: Yeah. Hi.
A: I'm Callum, I'm in St Helens. You?
B: Dominic. Walthamstow.
A: London, nice. Sorry, I've got to ask, are you on nights as well? You look about as knackered as I feel.
B: [laughs] No. Just, er, a long week. I run a post-production company, so it's sort of ten till ten when it's busy.
A: Ten till ten, that's worse than my shifts to be fair. What's post-production, like editing and that?
B: Yeah. Editing, colour grading, sound. Mostly adverts. Someone shoots it, we make it look like it was meant to look.
A: That's class, that. Have I seen anything you've done?
B: Probably. There was a supermarket Christmas one with a fox in the snow.
A: No way, with the little fox? Megan, me wife, she cried at that. Proper cried.
B: That was the idea, yeah. Good to know it worked on someone.
A: She'll be made up when I tell her. What's that print behind you? The orange one.
B: Oh. Screen print, limited run, from a studio in Hackney. I haven't hung it yet. Bought it last week and I probably shouldn't have, if I'm honest.
A: Ha, that's how Megan talks about my running trainers. It looks good though. I'm not really arty, but I like a wander round the Walker or Tate Liverpool. I usually drag someone with me.
B: Tate Liverpool's alright actually. Good building.
A: It's an old warehouse on the docks, isn't it? I'm more into the history bit to be fair. I listen to loads of podcasts on the drive to work, Titanic, Industrial Revolution, all that.
B: What's the drive to?
A: The glassworks. I'm on the float line. Erm, so the molten glass comes out the furnace onto a bath of molten tin and floats flat. I'm on the hot end, so I'm checking temperatures and thickness and spotting defects before it gets anywhere near a window.
B: Huh. That's sort of what a colourist does, in a way. Watching a monitor all night for the bit that's wrong.
A: Yeah, do you know what I mean, it's the same thing! Hours of nothing and then one little flaw and it all goes off.
B: Yeah. The flaw's always on the last day, as well.
A: Every time. So do you get to watch much telly and films yourself, or are you sick of it?
B: No, I go to the cinema a lot. On my own, mostly. Small places, the Prince Charles, the BFI. Saw a Korean thriller last week that was, er, quite good.
A: Quite good, or actually good?
B: [laughs] Actually good. Best thing I've seen this year. It's set in one flat, basically, and by the end you're scared of the fridge.
A: Scared of the fridge! I'd watch that. Megan makes me watch Love Island, so anything's an upgrade, mate.
B: That's a low bar.
A: It's on the floor. Do you follow any sport, or is it just films?
B: Charlton. Because of my dad. They lost on Saturday, obviously.
A: Ah, I'm Saints, rugby league. Season ticket with me dad and me brother, same seats for years. It's the dads, isn't it, they get you young.
B: Yeah. No way out once they've done it.
A: None. What's the film called anyway? I'll put it on the—
